cards.method: Quantifying QUALITATIVE survey expectations (up/same/down shares -> a numeric expectations series): the balance approach, Carlson-Parkin (+limen/distribution extensions), the regression approach, conditional expectations
cards.when: you have a QUALITATIVE expectations survey (the shares/counts of respondents expecting a rise/no change/a fall in a macro variable y, typically inflation) + the ACTUAL series y, and you want a NUMERIC series of quantified expectations for downstream analysis/charts
cards.when_not: QUANTITATIVE expectations that are already numeric (survey point forecasts) -> analyse them directly; density or fan-chart forecasts -> category 12; anchoring or disagreement regressions -> #33, or plain OLS; data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.criterion: you want the simplest indicator: a scaling of the balance (up-down) with theta calibrated to the actual change in y; minimal distributional assumptions
you want the probability method with indifference limens; limen_type selects Carlson-Parkin, Weber-Fechner, a constant, or a symmetric or asymmetric series, and distrib_type the normal, logistic or t
you want time-invariant ASYMMETRIC upper and lower limens estimated by OLS, plus a symmetry test (White, or the small-sample heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors)
you want a method with NO assumption of symmetric/parametric limens: expectations built on the empirical distribution of past realizations (a moving/fixed experience horizon)

output_key_fields: qn_balance: y_e_mean_abs / y_e_mean_perc (chart-data: the quantified expectation in levels, the abs & the perc version) + delta_y_e_mean/sd_abs/perc + theta_abs/theta_perc (the scaling) + nob/mae/rmse
qn_carlson_parkin: y_e_mean_abs/perc (chart-data) + limen_abs/limen_perc (the indifference limen per period) + delta_y_e_* + nob/mae/rmse + the limen_type/distrib_type echo
qn_regression: y_e_mean_abs/perc (chart-data) + upper_limen_abs/lower_limen_abs (+perc) + symmetry_abs/symmetry_perc (the p-value of the symmetry test) + nob/mae/rmse
qn_conditional_expectations: y_e (chart data — the quantified expectation, full length and blank outside the window) plus nob/mae/rmse and the exp_horizon_type and distrib_param echo
all of them: the forecast_horizon/first_period/last_period echo of the period window
interpretation_traps: abs vs perc: each of bal/cp/ra gives TWO versions — expectations of the ABSOLUTE change (y_e_mean_abs) vs of the PERCENTAGE change (y_e_mean_perc); choose according to whether the question concerns a level or a rate
y_e is full-length and aligned to the input, blank outside [first_period, last_period]; nob counts only the quantified periods — do not confuse the length of y_e with nob

the shares must be NON-NEGATIVE: the raw routine SILENTLY accepts negative shares and produces plausible-but-wrong output (the balance theta came out inflated) -> a hard gate requires up, same and down to be non-negative; they need not sum to 100, since 'Don't know' is allowed
cp does NOT need first_period>forecast_horizon (source-verified: cp calibrates against the FUTURE change y[t+h] vs y[t]); the ONLY constraint is last_period+forecast_horizon<=n

qn_conditional_expectations degenerates when the experience window is too short: it SILENTLY returns nob=0, or an entirely blank y_e; the fix is for fix_horizon_end to reach roughly first_period-1. A post-check gate blocks it, and an even shorter window raises an internal error

the DISTRIBUTION root: the Carlson-Parkin and regression routes with distrib_type='t' need distrib_t_df>0, defaulting to last minus first; the logistic uses a location and a scale, the normal a mean and a standard deviation
DETERMINISM: analytic/OLS methods, NO RNG (identical verified) -> no seed
sources: the balance, Carlson-Parkin, regression-adjusted and cross-entropy quantifiers (arguments and value fields verified live)
Batchelor, R.A. (1984) 'Quantitative vs. qualitative measures of inflation expectations' Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 48(2) 99-120 (the balance approach)
Carlson, J.A. & Parkin, M. (1975) 'Inflation expectations' Economica 42, 123-138 (the Carlson-Parkin probability method)
Henzel, S. & Wollmershaeuser, T. (2005) 'Quantifying inflation expectations with the Carlson-Parkin method' Journal of Business Cycle Measurement and Analysis 2, 321-352 (the Weber-Fechner limen)
Nardo, M. (2003) 'The quantification of qualitative survey data: a critical assessment' Journal of Economic Surveys 17(5) 645-668 (the zero-share correction)
Pesaran, M. (1984) 'Expectations formation and macroeconomic modelling' in Contemporary macroeconomic modelling, 27-55 (the regression approach)
MacKinnon, J.G. & White, H. (1985) 'Some heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance matrix estimators' Journal of Econometrics 29, 305-325 (the symmetry-test SE)
Zuckarelli, J. (2015) 'A new method for quantification of qualitative expectations' Economics and Business Letters 3(5) 123-128 (conditional expectations)

cards.method: Design-based complex-survey estimation (means/totals/quantiles/domains) with correct design variances (stratification, clustering, weights, fpc)
cards.when: estimating means/totals/quantiles/domains from survey microdata (expectation/consumer/business tendency surveys, e.g. Michigan, the ECB SPF) where the sampling DESIGN (strata/clusters/weights/fpc) must enter the variance; the naive s²/n understates it (clustering) or ignores the sampling weights -> a wrong CI
cards.when_not: informal or equally weighted data with no design (a plain mean or quantile); a regression on a survey design (a future node); calibration, post-stratification, raking, or a replicate-weight bootstrap (a different family); estimating category proportions, which changes the output shape; time-series or aggregate data rather than microdata; qualitative tendency surveys (-> #231) or small-area estimation (-> #233)

alternatives.criterion: ALWAYS FIRST: declare the complex-survey design from a df_handle + column names (ids/strata/weights/probs/fpc); ids='1' => no clusters; it returns a raw_handle that feeds the consumers
you want the design-based weighted MEAN of numeric variables + a correct SE/CI/cv/deff
you want an estimate of a population TOTAL (a weighted sum) + a design SE
you want weighted QUANTILES (the median etc.) with a design CI/SE; the quantiles must lie strictly in (0,1)
you want an estimate per DOMAIN/subgroup (a mean or a total per level of a grouping variable) with a correct design SE per domain

output_key_fields: srv_design: design (register -> a raw_handle) + metadata (n_obs, n_variables, numeric_vars, n_strata, has_strata/has_fpc/has_clusters, weighted, weight_min/max/mean/total = a summary of the design weights 1/prob)

srv_mean/srv_total: an estimates df {variable, estimate, SE, cv, ci_lower, ci_upper[, deff]} + coefficients + SE + vcov (a matrix with axis labels) + statistic('mean'/'total') + the raw fit (to_mcp -> a stub)
srv_quantile: an estimates df {variable, quantile, estimate, SE, ci_lower, ci_upper} (newsvyquantile: a matrix per variable, with columns quantile/ci.2.5/ci.97.5/se) + n_quantiles
srv_by_domain: an estimates df (records per domain, with the columns produced by svyby: the grouping + estimate + se) + n_groups + group_levels + statistic
interpretation_traps: the design effect is Var_design/Var_SRS; above 1 it means clustering or unequal weighting INCREASES the variance relative to a simple random sample of the same n; the column appears ONLY when deff=True
weights AND probs are mutually exclusive (probs = 1/weights); with neither => an equally weighted SRS (weight_min==weight_max); non-positive weights -> a hard gate (invalid estimates)
nest=True applies ONLY when the cluster ids are reused within strata, so that they need relabelling per stratum; otherwise the strata come out wrong

svyquantile (survey 4.5 'newsvyquantile'): a list per variable, matrix columns {quantile, ci.2.5, ci.97.5, se}, row labels=the probs; quantiles of 0/1 -> infinities -> a gate (strictly (0,1)); in small samples the CI can be NaN (the linearization df) -> to_mcp maps them to null
the variables MUST be numeric: a categorical one would give PROPORTIONS per level, a different output shape -> a hard gate here rejects non-numeric variables

the finite population correction REDUCES the standard error when the sample is a large fraction of the population; leaving it unset means sampling with replacement — no correction, and a conservative standard error
PURELY ANALYTIC (Horvitz-Thompson/linearization) -> no RNG/seed; identical output across two calls (a seed would be needed only for a replicate-weights bootstrap, which is out of scope)
sources: the complex-survey estimators (design, mean, total, quantile, by-group, standard error, CV, design effect) (live-verified, the engine)
Lumley 2010 'Complex Surveys: A Guide to Analysis Using the reference' (Wiley) — design-based estimation, design effects, domain estimation
Lumley 2004 JSS 9(1) (analysis of complex survey samples)
Horvitz & Thompson 1952 JASA 47:663-685 (the design-based estimator of totals)

cards.method: Small-area estimation (SAE): the Fay-Herriot area-level EBLUP (+ the analytic Prasad-Rao MSE) & the Battese-Harter-Fuller unit-level EBLUP
cards.when: estimating an indicator per small area/domain (regions, age/subgroups of a survey) when the per-area sample is too small for a reliable DIRECT estimate -> 'borrowing strength' through a model of auxiliary variables + a random effect; eblupFH when you have ONLY aggregate direct estimates + their sampling variances (area level); eblupBHF when you have UNIT-level micro data + the population means of the auxiliary variables (unit level); mseFH for an analytic MSE/CV of reliability
cards.when_not: large per-area samples (the direct estimate suffices); unknown sampling variances for FH; spatial/spatio-temporal correlation between areas (eblupSFH/eblupSTFH, separate methods); non-normal/EB under a transformation (ebBHF); a plain regression with no domain structure

alternatives.criterion: you have ONE direct estimate theta_hat_i per area + its sampling VARIANCE psi_i (vardir); you want a shrinkage estimate (a point estimate)

alternatives.alt: sae_mse_fh (the FH EBLUP + an analytic MSE + CV%)
alternatives.criterion: you want ALSO the analytic (Prasad-Rao g1+g2+g3) MSE/RMSE estimate + the CV% for reliability per area (with an optional seeded bootstrap goodness-of-fit test, B>0)
you have UNIT-level micro data (a nested-error regression) + the population means/sizes of the auxiliary variables per area; you want the EBLUP of the area MEANS

output_key_fields: eblup: a numeric vector of small-area estimates (chart-data); direct: the direct estimates (the model response); n_areas/n_domains
coefficients (FH): a data_frame {beta,std_error,tvalue,pvalue}; fixed (BHF): a named beta vector
variance components: refvar (the between-area sigma_u^2); errorvar (the within-area sigma_e^2, BHF); icc = refvar/(refvar+errorvar) (BHF); convergence/iterations/goodness (loglike/AIC/BIC/KIC, FH)
sae_mse_fh: mse (a numeric vector; Prasad-Rao) + cv = 100*sqrt(mse)/eblup (the CV%); bootstrap = B
sae_eblup_bhf: domain/sampsize/random(u_i)/residuals/loglike (the heavy merMod summary is deliberately removed)
interpretation_traps: vardir is the sampling VARIANCE (SD^2), NOT the SD -> the wrong scale gives silently wrong shrinkage; the wrapper blocks vardir<0 (a hard gate) because eblupFH accepts negative values and returns an apparently valid EBLUP
sae_eblup_bhf: when a target area is missing from the population means or sizes, the routine emits ONLY a warning and silently returns a blank EBLUP -> a hard gate on full coverage

vardir and dom are resolved as column NAMES when data is supplied, so they must be given as strings rather than as expressions or values; the wrapper copies them into fixed sae_vardir and sae_dom columns

the EBLUP = a shrinkage gamma_i*direct + (1-gamma_i)*regression with gamma_i = A/(A+psi_i); areas with a large psi_i (a small sample) shrink more towards the model; read the CV% per area for reliability
seed: only the bootstrap goodness-of-fit path (B>0) in mseFH/eblupFH is stochastic; the EBLUP/analytic MSE are deterministic (identical when seeded, verified)
sources: the small-area estimators (Fay-Herriot EBLUP, its MSE, and the unit-level BHF EBLUP)
Molina & Marhuenda 2015, small-area estimation, 7(1) 81-98
Fay & Herriot 1979 'Estimates of Income for Small Places: An Application of James-Stein Procedures to Census Data' JASA 74(366) 269-277 (area-level FH)
Battese, Harter & Fuller 1988 'An Error-Components Model for Prediction of County Crop Areas Using Survey and Satellite Data' JASA 83(401) 28-36 (unit-level BHF)
Prasad & Rao 1990 'The Estimation of the Mean Squared Error of Small-Area Estimators' JASA 85(409) 163-171 (the analytic MSE)
Rao & Molina 2015 'Small Area Estimation' 2nd ed, Wiley (the textbook)

cards.method: Categorical association / contingency tables: a chi-squared test of independence, Fisher's exact test, nominal vs ordinal association measures with CIs
cards.when: TWO CATEGORICAL answers PER RESPONDENT in a cross-section survey (e.g. a price expectation up/=/down x a plan for a major purchase): the contingency table + sparsity diagnostics (ca_contingency) -> an independence test (ca_chisq if Cochran's rule passes; ca_fisher if it does not) -> the SIZE of the relation with measures + CIs (ca_associations)
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES / time-dependent data (a hard cross-section gate — see the #257 preconditions; the HAC path: sandwich, cat 07); CONTINUOUS variables (discretise first: c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column); QUANTIFICATION of survey balance/Carlson-Parkin shares -> #237 quantification; weighted survey designs (weights/strata/clusters) -> survey (svychisq); STRATIFIED / >=3-dimensional tables (mantelhaen/loglin); a CONTINUOUS vs CATEGORICAL comparison of means -> #250 tests-parametric / #251 tests-nonparametric; charts (the frontend, §5)

alternatives.criterion: cochran_ok=False — an expected count below 1, or more than 20% of the cells below 5 — ⇒ an EXACT test instead of the asymptotic chi-squared; a 2x2 table ALSO yields an odds ratio with its interval

alternatives.alt: ca_chisq with simulate_p_value=True and a seed
alternatives.criterion: a sparse AND large table where the exact Fisher test fails («FEXACT error 5/6/7») ⇒ a Monte-Carlo p-value (r2dtable, seeded)
the codes ENCODE AN ORDER (Likert/up-=-down) ⇒ Gamma/Kendall tau-b/Stuart tau-c/Somers' D; on a NOMINAL scale they are uninterpretable (this is NEVER guessed)
ONE of the variables is CONTINUOUS (a comparison of means/medians per group) rather than two categorical ones
a weighted/complex sample (weights/strata/clusters) ⇒ the Rao-Scott correction; #257 presupposes a SIMPLE random sample

output_key_fields: ca_contingency: counts/expected (r x c) + prop_total/prop_row/prop_col + row_sums/col_sums + min_expected/n_cells_below_1/n_cells_below_5/share_below_5 + cochran_ok/strict_ok (THE ROUTING CRITERION chi-squared vs Fisher)

ca_chisq: statistic (OF THE TEST — Yates-corrected when correct=True AND the table is 2x2) / statistic_pearson (ALWAYS the UNCORRECTED Pearson X²) / df / p_value / significant / decision + cramers_v (ALWAYS computed from statistic_pearson ⇒ IDENTICAL to the Cramér's V of ca_associations) + residuals (Pearson) / stdres (approximately standard normal) / contribution / contribution_share (the share of statistic_pearson, which ALWAYS sums to 1) PER CELL — the chart data showing which cell «drives» the X² — plus yates_requested and yates_applied
ca_fisher: p_value/decision + odds_ratio/odds_ratio_lwr/odds_ratio_upr/conf_level (2x2 ONLY, conditional MLE) + is_2x2 + workspace or (simulate_p_value, B, seed)

ca_associations: the nominal block {cramers_v, contingency_coef, tschuprows_t, uncertainty_coef_sym/row/col, gk_tau_row/col}, each as (estimate, lower, upper); phi for a 2x2 table ONLY, and absent otherwise; gamma on the ordinal scale ONLY; plus the full 16-by-3 or 9-by-3 association matrix, with assocs_measures and ordinal_excluded

ALL: x_codes/y_codes + x_labels/y_labels (EXTERNALIZATION OF THE CODING — §3b gate 6) + n/n_input/n_na/na_action + cross_section_gate {lb_statistic, lb_p_value, lb_lag, n, n_na, alpha, tested, decision}
interpretation_traps: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (cross-section only): EVERY function calls the SHARED cross-section gate (the shared gates module) on the ORIGINAL vectors — an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type, plus a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5); autocorrelation INFLATES the Type I error ⇒ a spuriously significant chi-squared. That is why the input is VECTORS OF OBSERVATIONS rather than a ready-made contingency table: the whiteness statistic is not defined on an aggregated table

gate_alpha (default 0.05) — DECOUPLED FROM THE TEST'S alpha: alpha exists ONLY in ca_chisq/ca_fisher (the only ones with a decision); ca_contingency/ca_associations do NOT expose it at all (it would be a silent no-op). The Ljung-Box precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha ⇒ by construction it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input; LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1%, n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for 0.01/0.05/0.10

ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: survey answers are the permutable population par excellence, yet a SORTED file makes the whiteness check reject (live-verified), whereas the chi-square, the exact test and Cramér's V are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT, since the contingency table does not change. ordered=False omits the whiteness check explicitly (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered'), while the structural checks and the time-indexed-type rejection (branch='class-rejected') stay ALWAYS active. Supplying lb_lag together with ordered=False is a hard stop

SILENTLY WRONG: chisq_test with expected counts < 5 emits ONLY the warning «Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect» and returns a p-value ⇒ OUR OWN HARD gate (rule='cochran' by default: none < 1 AND <=20% of the cells < 5; rule='strict': none < 5) that routes to ca_fisher / simulate_p_value

SILENTLY WRONG: a ONE-row/one-column table ⇒ chisq_test switches SILENTLY to a «Chi-squared test for given probabilities» (goodness-of-fit, df = c-1) — A DIFFERENT TEST; gated with >=2 levels + a post-check df == (r-1)(c-1)

SILENTLY WRONG: cross-tabulation drops the gaps SILENTLY ⇒ an explicit policy, na_action='fail' by default or 'omit' PAIRWISE, with n_input and n_na always in the output; a ZERO MARGIN — an empty row or column — gives a NaN statistic and a blank p with ONLY a warning, and a cryptic type error inside Cramér's V ⇒ a hard gate

A CATEGORICAL INPUT (the most frequent wrong type in a categorical node) ⇒ a hard stop with an EDUCATIONAL message: it names the argument, reports the dtype and the level count — never the storage mode, which live-verified LIES, since a categorical stores as numeric and yet is not numeric — and gives the EXPLICIT conversion to integer codes 1..k in level order, with the level names becoming the labels. The node requires NUMERICALLY CODED VECTORS OF OBSERVATIONS, a requirement of the shared cross-section gate

SILENTLY WRONG: phi on an r x c table does NOT error — it returns sqrt(X²/n), which EXCEEDS 1 (a perfect 3x3 gives 1.414214); it is exposed ONLY for 2x2. Likewise the Yates correction is ignored SILENTLY outside 2x2, so yates_applied reports what ACTUALLY happened; in ca_associations, correct=True outside 2x2 is a hard stop

YATES AGAINST EFFECT SIZE (CRITICAL): Cramér's V is defined (Cramér 1946 §21.9) on the UNCORRECTED Pearson X² — NOT on the Yates-corrected statistic that is the conventional DEFAULT for a 2x2 table (correct=True). The node ALWAYS computes the SIZE measures from statistic_pearson, INDEPENDENTLY of the correction, so that the Cramér's V of ca_chisq COINCIDES — within 1e-12, pinned in a regression test — with the one of ca_associations. LIVE (2x2, n=120): 0.5009034 from the Yates statistic against 0.5175817 from the Pearson one, a 4.4% UNDERSTATEMENT and TWO different numbers for ONE named statistic. Likewise contribution_share is divided by statistic_pearson, which otherwise summed to 1.0678, giving «shares» above 100%. On the Monte-Carlo path the correction is switched off, so the statistic and the Pearson statistic coincide

SILENTLY WRONG: the exact test on an r x c table ignores the alternative SILENTLY — live, a 3x3 with a one-sided alternative gave THE SAME p-value as the two-sided one ⇒ one-sided is allowed ONLY for 2x2, and it is incompatible with simulate_p_value, which is always two-sided

ORDINAL vs NOMINAL: the ordinal measures (Gamma/Kendall tau-b/Stuart tau-c/Somers' D/Pearson/Spearman) change SIGN with the arbitrary order of the categories ⇒ scale='nominal' is the SAFE default and excludes them explicitly (ordinal_excluded). NOTE: the Goodman-Kruskal TAU is a NOMINAL PRE measure (not Kendall's/Stuart's tau) and is ALWAYS returned

THE EXACT NETWORK ALGORITHM allocates its memory up front: a 4x4 table with n=300 fails at the default workspace («FEXACT error 6. LDKEY=620 is too small»); SOME such tables pass with a ten-fold workspace while DENSER ones fail there too («FEXACT error 7»); and a 12x12 fails even at 2e8 ⇒ the only remaining route is simulate_p_value=True, seeded. The node translates the cryptic message into an educational one with the two ways out; and there is a level cap, max_levels, defaulting to 20 within a permitted [2,50]

§3b gate 6 (fit/apply externalization): the node does NOT fit/transform, but it EXTERNALIZES THE CODING — x_codes/y_codes (numeric) + x_labels/y_labels are ALWAYS returned and handed back as x_levels/y_levels in the survey's next wave ⇒ tables COMPARABLE cell by cell. If binning preceded it, bn_apply keeps THE SAME breaks

DETERMINISM: all the default paths are algebraic — and the 'fisher' interval method for Cramér's V is Fisher's z transformation, not a simulation; the TWO Monte-Carlo paths seed the generator AND restore the caller's state afterwards; and the association matrix is PINNED to its most verbose form, since the lower settings return only 3 of the 16 measures and would change the SHAPE of the output
sources: Cochran, W.G. (1954) «Some Methods for Strengthening the Common Chi-Squared Tests», Biometrics 10(4):417-451 — the rule «no expected count < 1, <= 20% of the cells < 5»
Cramér, H. (1946) Mathematical Methods of Statistics, §21.9 — Cramér's V
Goodman, L.A. & Kruskal, W.H. (1954) «Measures of Association for Cross Classifications», JASA 49:732-764 — tau (a NOMINAL PRE measure) and gamma (ORDINAL)
Agresti, A. (2013) Categorical Data Analysis, 3rd ed., ch. 2-3 — nominal vs ordinal measures; why the ordinal ones are uninterpretable on a nominal scale
Fisher, R.A. (1935) The Design of Experiments, ch. II — the exact test

the chisq_test routine's documentation / the fisher_test routine — «For 2 by 2 tables, the null of conditional independence is equivalent to the hypothesis that the odds ratio equals one»; the warning-only behaviour with expected counts < 5; workspace/FEXACT

the association-measures reference — Cramér's V, the contingency coefficient, Tschuprow's T, phi, the uncertainty coefficient, the Goodman-Kruskal tau and gamma, and the full 16-by-3 association matrix
the normative gate spec §3b normative gate 4 (cross-section only); Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4 — the rule lag = min(10, n/5) of the Ljung-Box precheck

c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column.bn_quantile_bins # a CONTINUOUS variable -> INTEGER codes BEFORE the node (bn_apply for the 2nd wave, THE SAME breaks)

cards.method: Fitting continuous densities to probability bins
cards.when: surveys report probabilities over intervals, and almost every use of them needs a continuous density
cards.when_not: the respondent used one or two bins only, where a continuous fit is not identified

alternatives.criterion: the standard for bounded support
few bins, symmetric responses
many bins and no shape assumption wanted

output_key_fields: params: fitted distribution parameters per respondent
moments: mean, variance and skewness implied
fit_quality: how well the fitted density reproduces the reported bins
n_bins_used: respondents with too few bins to fit
interpretation_traps: RESPONDENTS USING ONE OR TWO BINS CANNOT SUPPORT A TWO-PARAMETER FIT; the convention of assigning a triangular or uniform density to them is an assumption that affects aggregate uncertainty measures
open-ended end bins require an assumption about their extent, and that assumption drives the variance
the aggregate density is the average of individual densities, which is not the density of the average
sources: Engelberg, Manski & Williams 2009 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 27:30-41)
Zarnowitz & Lambros 1987 (Journal of Political Economy 95:591)

cards.method: Disagreement and uncertainty from density forecasts
cards.when: survey densities contain two distinct things -- how uncertain each forecaster is, and how much they differ -- and conflating them is common
cards.when_not: only point forecasts are available, where uncertainty cannot be measured at all

alternatives.criterion: disagreement only, the common proxy
uncertainty only
both, plus their sum

output_key_fields: disagreement: variance of individual means
uncertainty: average individual variance
aggregate_variance: the sum, which is the variance of the aggregate density
correlation: between the two series over time
interpretation_traps: DISAGREEMENT IS NOT UNCERTAINTY: forecasters can agree precisely while all being very uncertain, and the dispersion of point forecasts measures only the first
the aggregate density's variance is the SUM of the two components, which is why using disagreement alone understates aggregate uncertainty
panel composition changes over time and moves disagreement without any change in beliefs
sources: Giordani & Soderlind 2003 (European Economic Review 47:1037-1059)
Lahiri & Sheng 2010 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 25:514)

cards.when: testing whether survey expectations are unbiased and efficient, and whether forecasters update sluggishly
cards.when_not: the survey panel is too short; the forecast target is ambiguous

alternatives.criterion: unbiasedness and efficiency
information rigidity from forecast revisions
efficiency against a specific information set

output_key_fields: mz: unbiasedness and efficiency test
cg_coefficient: the error-on-revision coefficient measuring rigidity
implied_rigidity: the implied Kalman gain or attention parameter
individual_vs_consensus: rigidity at both levels, which differ
interpretation_traps: THE COIBION-GORODNICHENKO COEFFICIENT ON CONSENSUS DATA MEASURES INFORMATION RIGIDITY; the same regression on INDIVIDUAL data measures something different and is often negative -- the two must not be conflated
overlapping forecast horizons induce serial correlation, so HAC standard errors are required
rejecting rationality can reflect an asymmetric loss function rather than irrationality
sources: Coibion & Gorodnichenko 2015 (American Economic Review 105:2644-2678)
Mincer & Zarnowitz 1969 (Economic Forecasts and Expectations)
statsmodels

cards.method: Survey weighting: raking, post-stratification and trimming
cards.when: the achieved sample does not match the population, and weights must be built and controlled before any estimate is produced
cards.when_not: the sample is a census; the population totals are unreliable

alternatives.criterion: few, well-populated cells
several marginal totals to match at once
extreme weights must be prevented

output_key_fields: weights: the final weights
design_effect: the variance inflation the weights cause
effective_sample_size: n over the design effect
trimmed: weights that hit the bounds
interpretation_traps: WEIGHTING TRADES BIAS FOR VARIANCE: a large design effect means the weights have cost you most of your sample, and the effective sample size is what should be reported
raking to inconsistent margins does not converge, and a truncated run silently returns weights matching nothing
trimming reduces variance and reintroduces the bias the weights were built to remove
sources: Deville & Sarndal 1992 (JASA 87:376-382)
Kish 1992 (Journal of Official Statistics 8:183)
Valliant, Dever & Kreuter 2018, Practical Tools for Designing and Weighting Survey Samples
svy

cards.method: Ordinal and rank agreement: Kendall W, kappa, Cronbach alpha and polychoric
cards.when: measuring how consistently respondents or raters order or score the same items
cards.when_not: there is one rater; the scale is continuous and ordinary correlation applies

alternatives.criterion: agreement on rankings across several raters
categorical agreement corrected for chance
internal consistency of an ordinal scale

output_key_fields: statistic: the requested agreement measure
conf_int: interval, usually by bootstrap
pairwise: agreement per rater pair
polychoric: the latent correlation matrix for ordinal items
interpretation_traps: CRONBACH'S ALPHA RISES MECHANICALLY WITH THE NUMBER OF ITEMS and is not a measure of unidimensionality; a high alpha on a multidimensional scale is routine and meaningless
kappa is sensitive to the marginal distribution, so it can be low despite high raw agreement when one category dominates
Pearson correlation between ordinal items is attenuated; the polychoric correlation is what a factor analysis of ordinal items needs
sources: Kendall & Babington Smith 1939 (Annals of Mathematical Statistics 10:275-287)
Fleiss 1971 (Psychological Bulletin 76:378)
Cronbach 1951 (Psychometrika 16:297)
pingouin

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: Handle to a NUMERICALLY CODED VECTOR of OBSERVATIONS for the ROW variable (one INTEGER category code PER RESPONDENT; e.g. down=1, same=2, up=3). NOT the ready-made contingency table — the table is built by the node. NOT a CONTINUOUS variable (discretize first: 00-data-utilities/binning). NOT a factor (hard stop): give int(x) — codes 1..k in the order of the levels — and levels(x) as 'x_labels'. CROSS-SECTION ONLY: series handles ARE REJECTED and a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck runs.

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: Handle to the CORRESPONDING coded vector for the COLUMN variable. SAME length as 'x' — PAIRED answers from the SAME respondents.

arguments.name: x_name
arguments.description: LABEL of the ROW variable (NOT data; default 'x'). Used in the axis labels and in the cross-section gate's diagnostics. Must differ from 'y_name'.

arguments.name: y_name
arguments.description: LABEL of the COLUMN variable (NOT data; default 'y').

arguments.name: x_levels
arguments.description: OPTIONAL COMPLETE set of INTEGER codes of the row variable (e.g. [1,2,3,4] when one questionnaire option was NOT selected by anyone). Must be a SUPERSET of the observed codes — otherwise the categorical encoder would SILENTLY turn the observations into NA. Useful for IDENTICAL coding between two waves of the same survey (comparable cell-by-cell tables). Omitting it, the levels result from the OBSERVED codes.

arguments.name: y_levels
arguments.description: Same as 'x_levels', for the COLUMN variable.

arguments.name: x_labels
arguments.description: OPTIONAL category LABELS (NOT data), ONE-TO-ONE with the SORTED codes (e.g. ['down','same','up']). Must be unique and non-empty (duplicates WOULD MERGE categories). Default: '<x_name>=<code>'.

arguments.name: y_labels
arguments.description: Same as 'x_labels', for the COLUMN variable.

arguments.name: na_action
arguments.description: EXPLICIT NA policy (default 'fail' = hard stop). the cross-tabulation routine SILENTLY drops NA (NA dropped), so the reported n would not be the input's n. With 'omit' the removal happens EXPLICITLY PER PAIR and the count is returned (n_na).

arguments.name: max_levels
arguments.description: Maximum number of categories PER variable (default 20; permitted [2, 50]). Many levels => a sparse table (the chi-square approximation collapses) and the EXACT Fisher blows up ("FEXACT error"). It is ALSO a safety net against accidentally passing a CONTINUOUS variable.

arguments.name: lb_lag
arguments.description: Lag of the Ljung-Box whiteness precheck (cross-section gate). If omitted: the documented rule min(10, n/5) (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4). MUST be a positive integer < n.

arguments.name: gate_alpha
arguments.description: Level OF THE CROSS-SECTION GATE in the OPEN interval (0,1) — default 0.05. Rejection threshold ONLY of the Ljung-Box whiteness precheck. ⚠️ It IS a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha: it blocks, by construction, ~gate_alpha of the proportion of VALID i.i.d. input (live: n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1% at 0.01/0.05/0.10). Hence it is DECOUPLED from the test's 'alpha'.

arguments.name: ordered
arguments.description: EXPLICIT declaration: do the ROWS (observations) carry ORDER meaning? True (default, conservative) => the Ljung-Box precheck RUNS. False => genuine cross-section (EXCHANGEABLE rows — e.g. survey respondents) and the precheck is EXPLICITLY skipped (decision = 'pass-unordered'). ⚠️ Ljung-Box depends on ORDER — chi-square/Fisher do NOT. The rejection of series handles/series ALWAYS applies.

arguments.name: scale
arguments.description: MEASUREMENT SCALE of the categories — NEVER guessed (default 'nominal' = safe). With 'ordinal', the ORDINAL measures are added (Goodman-Kruskal Gamma, Kendall tau-b, Stuart tau-c, Somers' D, Pearson/Spearman correlation), which presuppose that the CODES ENCODE ORDER; on a nominal scale they are uninterpretable (the sign changes with the arbitrary order of the categories). CAUTION: Goodman-Kruskal TAU is a NOMINAL PRE measure and is ALWAYS returned.

arguments.name: conf_level
arguments.description: Confidence level of the CI of ALL the measures (default 0.95).

arguments.name: cramer_method
arguments.description: Confidence interval method of the Cramér's V (DescTools· default 'ncchisq' = non-central chi-square). 'fisher' is the Fisher z-transformation — NO simulation, all options are DETERMINISTIC. Does NOT change the estimate.

arguments.name: correct
arguments.description: Yates continuity correction on the chi-square-based measures (V / C / T; default False). Allowed ONLY in 2x2 — elsewhere the usual implementations ignore it SILENTLY, so this node errors explicitly instead.

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.description: Significance level OF THE TEST in the OPEN interval (0,1) — default 0.05. Determines ONLY the 'decision' field; it does NOT change the p-value and does NOT affect the cross-section gate (which has its OWN 'gate_alpha').

arguments.name: rule
arguments.description: Rule for ACCEPTABLE expected frequencies (HARD gate — the usual chi-square routines only warn that the approximation may be incorrect). 'cochran' (default): no expected value < 1 AND <= 20% of cells < 5 (Cochran 1954). 'strict': NO expected value < 5. Failure => use ca_fisher or simulate_p_value=True.

arguments.name: correct
arguments.description: Yates continuity correction (default True). Applies ONLY to 2x2 — elsewhere it is ignored SILENTLY by the usual routines; the output field 'yates_applied' says what ACTUALLY happened. AFFECTS ONLY 'statistic'/'p_value' (the TEST's statistic). THE SIZE MEASURES ARE NOT: 'cramers_v' and 'contribution_share' are ALWAYS computed from the UNCORRECTED Pearson X² ('statistic_pearson'; Cramér 1946 §21.9), so they COINCIDE with ca_associations.

arguments.name: simulate_p_value
arguments.description: Monte-Carlo p-value instead of the asymptotic/exact path (default False). It is the WAY OUT when the Cochran rule rejects the chi-square (it does not rely on the asymptotic) or when the exact Fisher does not fit in memory ("FEXACT error"). Requires a seed for determinism.

arguments.name: B
arguments.description: Monte-Carlo replications when simulate_p_value=True (default 2000; minimum 100). Ignored otherwise.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed of the Monte-Carlo path (default 1234). The call runs with the seed set AND restores the caller's RNG state => a REPRODUCIBLE p-value without contaminating the RNG stream. Ignored on the algebraic (deterministic) paths.

arguments.description: Cluster/PSU identifiers: "1" (or "0") for NO clusters (default), or the name(s) of cluster columns (multistage sampling, from the broadest to the narrowest stage).

arguments.name: strata
arguments.description: Stratification column names (one stratified estimator per stratum); None = no strata. Requires nest=True if the cluster ids are reused within strata.

arguments.name: weights
arguments.description: ONE sampling-weights column (design weight = 1/prob; positive, finite). Mutually exclusive with 'probs'. None & without probs => equal-weighted SRS.

arguments.name: probs
arguments.description: ONE column of selection probabilities in (0,1] (weights = 1/probs); mutually exclusive with 'weights'.

arguments.name: fpc
arguments.description: Finite population correction: column(s) with population size (or sampling fraction) per stage; reduces the SE when the sample is a large fraction of the population. None = with-replacement (without fpc).

arguments.name: nest
arguments.description: True => the cluster ids are nested within the strata (re-labelling per stratum). Default False.
